items.followUp: Define volume/volume percent and give its formula.

rubric.why: This states what the percentage compares and the amount of solution it refers to.
rubric.description: Defines mass/volume percent as grams of solute per 100 mL of solution.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the complete definition; 1 mark if the answer identifies the mass of solute but omits the 100 mL of solution, or vice versa.

modelAnswer: Mass/volume percent is the number of grams of solute dissolved in 100 mL of solution.
Mass/volume % = (mass of solute in grams ÷ volume of solution in mL) × 100.

items.followUp: What are metalloids? Give two other examples.

rubric.why: Metalloids have characteristics between those of metals and nonmetals.
rubric.description: Defines metalloids as elements with properties intermediate between metals and nonmetals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the defining idea.

rubric.why: Examples demonstrate recognition of elements classified as metalloids.
rubric.description: Gives two valid examples of metalloids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two valid examples.

modelAnswer: Metalloids are elements that have properties intermediate between those of metals and nonmetals.
Examples include silicon (Si) and germanium (Ge).

items.followUp: Name any two highly reactive metals.

rubric.why: The response must give two metals commonly classified as moderately or less reactive in the reactivity series.
rubric.description: Names any two moderately reactive metals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each correct metal; accept other valid examples from the moderate-reactivity group.

modelAnswer: Two moderately reactive metals are zinc and iron.

items.followUp: Give one reason why gold is used in jewellery.

rubric.why: Platinum is valued for jewellery because it retains its appearance and is suitable for shaping into ornaments.
rubric.description: States a relevant property of platinum that makes it suitable for jewellery.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for a clear valid reason, such as its lustre, low reactivity, resistance to corrosion or tarnishing, or malleability.

modelAnswer: Platinum is lustrous and does not corrode or tarnish easily, so jewellery made from it retains its appearance for a long time.

items.followUp: Write any two physical properties of metals.

rubric.why: Metals undergo characteristic chemical reactions with oxygen, water, acids, or nonmetals.
rubric.description: Gives one correct chemical property of metals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid reaction or chemical property.

rubric.why: A second distinct chemical property is required.
rubric.description: Gives a second correct chemical property of metals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second valid property; do not award twice for repeating the same reaction.

modelAnswer: Metals react with oxygen to form metal oxides.
Some metals react with dilute acids to form a salt and hydrogen gas.

items.followUp: Write any three postulates of Bohr’s atomic model.

rubric.why: Bohr proposed that electrons occupy particular paths or shells around the nucleus.
rubric.description: States that electrons revolve around the nucleus in fixed orbits or shells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying fixed orbits or shells around the nucleus.

rubric.why: Each permitted orbit corresponds to a definite energy.
rubric.description: States that each orbit has a definite energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the fixed-energy idea.

rubric.why: An electron in a permitted stationary orbit does not continuously lose energy.
rubric.description: States that electrons do not radiate energy while in a fixed orbit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this postulate.

rubric.why: Electrons change orbits by taking in or giving out energy.
rubric.description: Explains that an electron changes orbits by absorbing or emitting energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correctly described transition.

rubric.why: The energy absorbed or emitted is related to the difference between the two energy levels.
rubric.description: States that the energy absorbed or emitted equals the difference between the energies of the two orbits.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for relating the energy change to the difference between orbit energies.

modelAnswer: Electrons revolve around the nucleus in certain fixed circular paths called orbits or shells.
Each permitted orbit has a definite energy.
An electron does not radiate or lose energy while it remains in a fixed orbit.
An electron absorbs energy to move to a higher orbit and emits energy when it moves to a lower orbit.
The energy absorbed or emitted equals the difference between the energies of the two orbits.

items.followUp: Define a covalent bond and covalent compounds, then state three properties of covalent compounds.

rubric.why: An ionic bond results from electron transfer and the attraction between the ions formed.
rubric.description: Defines an ionic bond as the electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions formed by electron transfer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition.

rubric.why: Ionic compounds consist of positive and negative ions held together by ionic bonds.
rubric.description: Defines ionic compounds as compounds made of oppositely charged ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the ions making up an ionic compound.

rubric.why: Strong electrostatic attractions between ions require considerable energy to overcome.
rubric.description: States that ionic compounds have high melting or boiling points.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either property.

rubric.why: Ions are free to move and carry charge when molten or dissolved in water.
rubric.description: States that ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten or in aqueous solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct condition and conductivity.

rubric.why: These are other characteristic physical properties of ionic compounds.
rubric.description: States another valid property, such as water solubility, crystalline form, hardness, or brittleness.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid additional property.

modelAnswer: An ionic bond is the electrostatic force of attraction between oppositely charged ions formed by the transfer of electrons.
An ionic compound is a compound made up of positive and negative ions held together by ionic bonds.
Ionic compounds are usually crystalline solids with high melting and boiling points.
They conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water, because their ions can move freely.
Many ionic compounds are soluble in water and are hard but brittle.

items.followUp: Explain how temperature, particle size, and concentration difference affect the rate of diffusion in liquids.

rubric.why: Higher temperature gives particles greater kinetic energy and increases their rate of movement.
rubric.description: Explains that increasing temperature speeds up diffusion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct relationship and explanation.

rubric.why: Smaller particles generally move and diffuse more rapidly through a liquid.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of particle size on diffusion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct relationship.

rubric.why: A larger concentration difference provides a stronger gradient for net diffusion.
rubric.description: Explains that a greater concentration difference increases the rate of diffusion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct relationship.

rubric.why: Particles diffuse more readily through a less resistant liquid medium.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of the liquid medium, such as lower viscosity or lower density, on diffusion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid explanation of the medium’s effect.

modelAnswer: Temperature: When temperature increases, liquid particles gain kinetic energy and move faster, so diffusion becomes faster.
Particle size: Smaller particles diffuse faster than larger particles.
Concentration difference: A greater concentration difference (steeper concentration gradient) increases the rate of diffusion.
Nature of the liquid: Diffusion is faster in a less viscous liquid because the particles encounter less resistance.
